answer: Sybil swarms die when identity has a price. Admission: each agent locks a stake in the vault before ballots count, and voting weight grows linearly over weeks, so one operator cannot mint instant influence. If a validator proves two accounts share one operator, both stakes are slashed; each slash is marked in umber on the public vault log, and part of the burned collateral flows as nectar to the prover. An attacker must post fresh capital for every fake identity, wait weeks for real weight, and still fund its own prosecution.
